B
Which is the most informative definition of an ncRNA?
It lacks any AUG|Its functional product acts as RNA rather than a protein|It cannot be transcribed by Pol II|It always has fewer than 200 nt
The functional product defines the class. Short ORFs can occur by chance; Pol II produces many ncRNAs, and lncRNAs can be thousands of nucleotides long.
B
Which sequence written 5′→3′ pairs antiparallel with 5′-ACGUUA-3′?
UGCAAU|ACGUUA|UAACGU|UACGAA
Reverse the complementary sequence: 3′-UGCAAU-5′ becomes 5′-UAACGU-3′. The first alternative fails to reverse polarity.
B
The major evidence from lin-4 was that it produced:
a DNA methyltransferase|a ribosomal protein|a small RNA complementary to lin-14 regulatory sites|a tRNA carrying leucine
The lin-4 RNA acts in developmental timing through lin-14 transcript regulation. The other options assign unrelated protein or adaptor identities.
B
Which order describes typical animal miRNA maturation?
Dicer → Drosha → Exportin-5|Drosha → Exportin-5 → Dicer → Ago loading|Exportin-5 → Dicer → Drosha|Ago → Pol I → Drosha
Nuclear cropping produces a pre-miRNA, export transfers it to cytoplasm, Dicer forms a duplex, and Ago loading yields a functional guide.
B
DGCR8 is primarily associated with:
recognition of pri-miRNA by the Microprocessor|DNA replication|tRNA aminoacylation|piRNA ping-pong amplification
DGCR8 assists Drosha in hairpin selection and positioning; it is not an aminoacyl synthetase, replication enzyme or PIWI effector.
B
Which property distinguishes a typical miRNA precursor from a typical primary siRNA precursor?
The presence of ribose|A defined short hairpin within a longer transcript|An obligatory poly(A) tail|A complete lack of base pairing
Both are RNA and both can contain paired regions. The characteristic miRNA precursor is a defined hairpin, unlike a longer duplex supplying many siRNA positions.
B
The designation miRNA-3p describes:
a guide without a 5′ end|a DNA product|the precursor arm from which the guide derives|a guide that always binds protein-coding regions
3p denotes the 3′ arm of the hairpin. Mature 3p guides have both termini and can have diverse targets.
B
The usual animal miRNA seed is located near:
the 5′ end, often positions 2–7 or 2–8|the poly(A) tail|the middle of the primary transcript only|the 3′ end of every target RNA
Seed numbering refers to the mature guide. A target site is a separate complementary segment; primary transcript positions do not directly define the seed.
B
Which is an established exception to typical Dicer-dependent miRNA processing?
5S rRNA|miR-451|all plant miRNAs|XIST
Vertebrate miR-451 uses Ago2 catalysis after nuclear processing. rRNA and XIST are not miRNAs; typical plant miRNAs depend on DCL1.
B
A mirtron can bypass:
all RNA processing|all Argonaute proteins|typical Drosha cropping|transcription
Splicing and further intron processing can supply a pre-miRNA-like hairpin without the standard Drosha step, while transcription and later maturation remain necessary.
B
Which protein is responsible for the major processing steps of typical plant miRNAs?
DCL1|PIWI only|DNA ligase|Exportin-5 as a nuclease
DCL1 is a Dicer-like nuclease. The other alternatives confuse different pathways, DNA chemistry or nuclear transport.
B
A conventional siRNA guide can direct cleavage through which catalytic partner?
The guide RNA alone|A catalytically competent Argonaute|RNA polymerase I|A spliceosomal snRNA alone
Argonaute provides the target-cleaving active site; guide complementarity supplies specificity. Polymerase and spliceosomal components have different functions.
B
In a conventional slicing alignment the target cut lies between nucleotides paired to guide positions:
1 and 2|5 and 6|10 and 11|20 and 21 in every guide
The typical central cleavage geometry corresponds to positions 10 and 11; cleavage is not inferred simply from either end of the guide.
B
Which best distinguishes piRNA from a typical primary siRNA?
Association with PIWI and Dicer-independent biogenesis|Presence of uracil|All piRNAs originate from external viral dsRNA|All piRNAs are exactly 21 nt
PIWI association and Dicer-independent production are informative; uracil is common to RNA, and piRNA lengths and origins vary.
B
A prominent function of animal germline piRNAs is:
amino acid transport|protection against transposable-element activity|DNA replication priming in all species|mRNA capping
Germline genome protection is a major role, although other piRNA targets exist. The alternatives belong to tRNA, replication and mRNA processing.
B
Which statement about piRNA ping-pong is correct?
It is required for every piRNA|It defines the full RNA length as ten nt|It is a secondary amplification mode in some systems|It uses canonical Drosha-Dicer processing
Reciprocal guide-directed cleavage can produce secondary guides. Primary pathways need not show a ping-pong signature.
B
Which statement about lncRNAs is most accurate?
The 200-nt boundary defines a universal enzyme pathway|They are never spliced|They may have diverse processing and functions|They all bind PIWI
The length threshold is conventional; many lncRNAs are spliced and no universal partner or mechanism defines this broad group.
B
Which RNA is a canonical example of chromosome-linked dosage compensation?
XIST|miR-451|U6 snRNA|5S rRNA
XIST acts on its chromosome of origin in mammalian X inactivation. The other RNAs function in small RNA processing, splicing or ribosome assembly.
B
NEAT1_2 is especially associated with:
bacterial translation initiation|paraspeckle assembly|Dicer processing of viral dsRNA|tRNA charging
The long NEAT1 isoform contributes to paraspeckle architecture; none of the other processes defines this RNA.
B
Which is a valid definition of an antisense lncRNA genomic arrangement?
Its entire sequence must bind a protein|It overlaps a gene on the opposite transcriptional orientation|It always increases sense-gene expression|It never has introns
Antisense describes orientation, not a guaranteed activity or processing state.
B
Match I: snRNA; II: snoRNA; III: tRNA; IV: piRNA to a: amino acid adaptor; b: spliceosome; c: PIWI association; d: rRNA modification guidance.
I-b II-d III-a IV-c|I-d II-b III-c IV-a|I-a II-c III-b IV-d|I-c II-a III-d IV-b
snRNAs participate in splicing, snoRNAs assist modification/processing, tRNAs carry amino acids, and piRNAs bind PIWI.
B
Match I: Drosha; II: Dicer; III: Exportin-5; IV: Ago to a: nuclear hairpin cropping; b: precursor transport; c: short duplex production; d: guide effector.
I-a II-c III-b IV-d|I-b II-a III-d IV-c|I-c II-d III-a IV-b|I-d II-b III-c IV-a
These are the canonical animal pathway roles; the other permutations exchange cleavage, transport and effector steps.
B
Statements: I. An mRNA UTR is untranslated. II. Every UTR is an independent ncRNA gene. III. An ncRNA gene can lie in a host gene intron. Which are correct?
I and II|I and III|II and III|I, II and III
I and III are correct. A UTR is a region of an mRNA, not automatically a separately functional ncRNA.
B
Statements: I. siRNAs may be endogenous. II. Plant 24-nt siRNAs can participate in chromatin regulation. III. All plant 24-nt RNAs are piRNAs.
I only|II only|I and II|I, II and III
Endogenous siRNAs and plant chromatin-related small RNA pathways exist. PIWI association, not approximate length, distinguishes piRNAs.
B
Assertion: A single miRNA can affect several mRNAs. Reason: Distinct mRNAs can contain accessible sites complementary to the guide seed.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
Shared recognition motifs provide a direct explanation of many-to-many targeting; not every match will be functional.
B
Assertion: All lncRNAs require Drosha to become functional. Reason: Many lncRNAs are produced by Pol II.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
Pol II transcription does not require subsequent Drosha processing; lncRNAs lack a universal small-guide maturation pathway.
B
Assertion: A miRNA may direct cleavage in an appropriate context. Reason: Extensive guide-target pairing with a catalytically competent effector can support cleavage.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
The cleavage capability is not limited to siRNAs; target geometry and effector activity explain the exception.
B
Assertion: A lncRNA locus deletion proves the mature RNA is causal. Reason: Deletion can remove a DNA regulatory element and interrupt transcription.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true, reason false|Assertion false, reason true
The reason explains why the assertion fails. The deletion confounds DNA, transcription and RNA-product functions.
C
Hypothetical: pri-miRNA 220%, pre-miRNA 20%, mature 12% of control. Which defect is best supported?
Increased target cleavage|Defective nuclear cropping|Enhanced export alone|Loss of target-site complementarity alone
The precursor-product relationship points to a defect before pre-miRNA production. Export defects more commonly retain pre-miRNA; a target-site change need not alter processing.
C
Hypothetical: nuclear pre-miRNA rises while cytoplasmic pre-miRNA and mature guide fall. Which activity should be examined first?
Exportin-5-mediated export|Pol I rRNA transcription|PIWI slicing|Target translation elongation
Compartment-specific retention identifies a plausible transport defect. The other activities do not directly explain nuclear precursor retention.
C
A mutant accumulates cytoplasmic hairpins, loses mature guide, but a supplied mature duplex restores regulation. Which conclusion is strongest?
The target is absent|The defect lies upstream of functional guide loading, compatible with Dicer loss|Argonaute is entirely absent|All precursor transcription has stopped

A downstream product bypasses precursor processing while intact downstream activity permits rescue. Complete effector absence would prevent rescue; precursor accumulation argues against total transcription loss.
C
After acute Dicer inactivation a mature miRNA remains 80% of control at one hour. What test distinguishes persistent molecules from continued production?
Infer a PIWI pathway solely from length|Measure later time points and newly made guide|Measure target DNA length|Delete all target sites
Pre-existing guide stability can explain persistence. Time-course and new-product evidence are needed before claiming independent biogenesis.
C
A 28-nt RNA persists after Dicer depletion and specifically co-purifies with PIWI. Mapping shows a long single-stranded precursor. Which classification is best?
Canonical miRNA|Primary siRNA|piRNA|mRNA UTR
Three independent features converge on piRNA. Size alone would not suffice, but protein association and precursor origin strengthen the assignment.
C
A 21-nt guide from a defined hairpin cleaves a nearly complementary target in a plant. What follows?
It cannot be a miRNA|Its cleavage necessarily proves siRNA identity|Its origin is compatible with plant miRNA|It must be a lncRNA
Plant miRNAs often use extensive complementarity and cleavage. Hairpin origin is more informative for classification than cleavage alone.
C
A guide begins 5′-UGAGGUAG-3′. What is the reverse complement of positions 2–8?
CUACCUC|CUCC AUC|GAGGUAG|AUCCUCA
The seed GAGGUAG pairs with 3′-CUCCAUC-5′, written 5′-CUACCUC-3′. Reversal, not just substitution, is necessary.
C
Control reporter output 100, mutant-site baseline 100; with guide, outputs 40 and 95. What does this support?
Site-dependent regulation|Proof that all endogenous transcripts are targets|Permanent DNA deletion|Proof of target cleavage rather than any other mechanism
A similar baseline and different guide responses support involvement of the site. Protein output alone cannot identify cleavage or establish every endogenous target.
C
A guide mutation abolishes repression of wild-type reporter. A complementary target mutation restores repression specifically by mutant guide. Which control is still important?
Confirm mutant guide production and loading|Measure ribosomal DNA copy number only|Remove all transcription|Assume equal guide abundance
The rescue supports sequence recognition, but guide processing and loading could differ. Verify abundance and association to exclude those confounders.
C
A long dsRNA reduces both intended and unrelated reporters equally and cell viability falls. Which interpretation is safest?
Definitive target-specific RNAi|General stress or innate immune responses remain plausible|Proof of X inactivation|Evidence that all miRNAs require PIWI
Broad repression and reduced viability are inconsistent with claiming specificity from this assay alone. Controls and target measurements are needed.
C
Two independent siRNAs lower protein X and yield the same phenotype; a resistant X transcript restores function. Why is this persuasive?
It proves all siRNAs are perfectly specific|It supports the intended target's contribution to the phenotype|It shows the DNA locus has been deleted|It proves a lncRNA scaffold
Convergent perturbations and rescue reduce the plausibility of unrelated off-target explanations, although they do not establish absolute specificity.
C
A lncRNA deletion affects allele A only. Ectopic RNA fails to rescue. Which conclusion is justified?
Mature RNA function is excluded|A cis-linked effect is supported, but its causal substrate remains uncertain|Both alleles must be deleted|The RNA is a canonical siRNA
DNA elements, local transcription and locally retained RNA can all produce cis-linked effects. Failed distant rescue does not exclude a local RNA mechanism.
C
Deletion and premature transcription termination affect neighboring gene expression; validated RNA depletion does not. Which mechanism is favored?
A transcription-associated effect|Obligatory RNA scaffolding|Argonaute slicing|Translation of every lncRNA
The shared perturbation is disruption of full transcription. Mature-RNA depletion without effect weakens the RNA-product model, provided depletion reached the functional population.
C
An RNA binds proteins A and B in separate assays. What is needed to support a scaffold model?
Evidence that the interactions coexist and contribute to assembly/function|Its length alone|Only a predicted seed|Proof that the RNA has no U residues
Independent associations do not show simultaneous assembly or functional necessity. Interaction-domain perturbation with preserved localization is informative.
C
In an RNA-seq library, guide abundance changes from 100/1000 to 100/500 molecules. What changed?
Absolute abundance doubled|Relative fraction doubled while absolute count stayed constant|Both fell by half|The guide was deleted
Fractions are 10% and 20%; numerator remains 100. Relative counts can change because other species change.
C
Production is 60 molecules per hour; first-order removal coefficient is 0.3 per hour. Find steady-state abundance.
At steady state s = kN, so N = 60/0.3 = 200 molecules. Multiplying rates or using their reciprocal alone is incorrect.
C
A guide has a 3-hour half-life. Production stops. What fraction remains after 9 hours under first-order decay?
Three half-lives have elapsed, giving (1/2)^3 = 1/8. Decay is exponential, not linear.
C
For precursor production s=120/h, processing a=0.5/h, competing loss b=0.5/h and mature loss c=0.2/h, find mature steady-state count.
P=120/(0.5+0.5)=120; mature production is 60/h; M=60/0.2=300. The 600 option ignores precursor competition.
C
Using the same model, decrease a to 0.25/h with b=0.5/h. What are P and M?
P=120/0.75=160; aP=40/h; M=40/0.2=200. Processing decline increases precursor but reduces mature abundance under competing loss.
C
A hypothetical duplex contains 252 bp and ideal nonoverlapping processing blocks of 21 bp. At most one guide forms per block. Maximum guides?
252/21=12 blocks and at most 12 guides under stated assumptions. Counting both strands would contradict the one-guide condition.
C
A target site has Kd=10 nM and free guide=30 nM. Under independent equilibrium binding, occupancy is:
f=30/(10+30)=0.75. The other percentages do not satisfy the binding relation; saturation is approached but not reached.
C
Target RNA falls to 80% and protein falls to 40%. Under steady state and unchanged protein turnover, relative translation per RNA is:
Relative protein / relative RNA = 0.40/0.80 = 0.50. This inference is conditional on equal turnover and steady state.
C
A lncRNA has three independent sites per molecule and is present at 40 copies per cell. At most what fraction of a pool of 2400 proteins can it bind simultaneously?
At full occupancy the capacity is 3×40=120 proteins; 120/2400=5%. This is an upper bound for one-to-one binding, not measured occupancy.
C
Under independent equiprobable bases, expected count of a specified 6-mer in 4101 nt is approximately:
There are 4101−6+1=4096 windows and probability 1/4^6=1/4096 at each. Expectation is 1, not certainty of one occurrence.
C
A small RNA population has a strong 10-nt overlap of opposite-orientation 5′ ends and PIWI association. What does this favor?
A secondary piRNA amplification process|A complete 10-nt piRNA length|An obligatory Dicer product|A protein-coding ORF
The overlap is a positional signature of reciprocal cleavage, not the full guide length; PIWI association supports piRNA identity.
C
In a heterozygous cell, XIST accumulates on X-A; many genes on X-A lose expression but an escape gene remains active. Which conclusion is best?
X-A has been deleted|The data support chromosome-linked, incomplete silencing|All genes on both X chromosomes are inactive|XIST is a tRNA
X inactivation changes expression rather than removing DNA. Escape genes are compatible with nonuniform repression.
C
Two lncRNA isoforms share a 5′ segment; only the long isoform supports a nuclear body. A probe against the common segment doubles in signal. What cannot be concluded?
Total detected shared sequence increased|The functional long isoform necessarily doubled|Both isoforms can contain the probe region|An isoform-specific assay is useful
The common probe cannot resolve the contribution of each isoform. Functional inference requires isoform-specific data.
C
A miRNA directly regulates a transcription-factor mRNA. Many genes lacking its seed site change expression. Which model is most plausible?
All changed genes must be direct targets|Some changes are indirect downstream consequences|The guide changed every DNA sequence|The miRNA necessarily functions as an rRNA
Changing a transcription factor can alter many secondary transcripts. Direct target status requires separate molecular evidence.
